key_insight: A 24-arm fractal vane produces nearly axisymmetric yielding, while simulation-informed conversion expressions improve rheological interpretation beyond the circular Couette analogy.
engineering_relevance: Improved torque-to-stress and rotation-to-strain-rate conversions support more accurate material characterization in vane-in-cup rheometers.
method: Model viscoplastic fluids using the Herschel–Bulkley constitutive law.
Use augmented Lagrangian finite elements in 2D and regularised finite volumes in 3D.
Compare 4-arm, 6-arm and 24-arm fractal vanes to assess yielding and refine conversion closures.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports extensive 2D and 3D simulations across a broad parameter range, but provides no quantitative accuracy metrics or experimental validation.
watch_item: This is a computational rheometry study, not an AI surrogate model; closure applicability beyond the simulated configurations requires verification.
paper_title: Three-dimensional computational rheometry of viscoplastic fluids in vane-in-cup fixtures
